records.Entity / project type: Bitcoin protocol library / Rust crate ecosystem
records.Concise description: A maintained Rust library and crate ecosystem for Bitcoin network protocol primitives, transactions, scripts, keys, serialization, and application development.
records.Deeper researched summary: rust-bitcoin is both the main `bitcoin` Rust crate and a broader community of related crates. The core library supports Bitcoin network protocol types and associated primitives used throughout Rust Bitcoin software. MSC profiles the main rust-bitcoin ecosystem as one canonical developer-infrastructure entity while keeping narrower companion crates such as rust-miniscript relational unless a future registry needs a separate profile.
records.Launch / history: rust-bitcoin has been developed for more than a decade and remains actively maintained in 2026, with current documentation describing a maintained core-crate set and ecosystem standards.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the most important reusable protocol libraries for modern Bitcoin software and underlies wallets, node clients, Lightning components, and developer tooling.
records.Verification basis: Current project-controlled site and organization documentation establish maintained protocol-library scope and the relationship to companion crates.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not create a profile for every rust-bitcoin crate; rust-miniscript remains relationship-only in the initial canon.
Library correctness and downstream application security are separate from Bitcoin consensus governance.

records.Concise description: Bitcoin Core's high-performance, high-assurance C library for secp256k1 elliptic-curve operations used throughout Bitcoin software.
records.Deeper researched summary: libsecp256k1 implements optimized elliptic-curve operations on the secp256k1 curve, including signature verification/signing-related primitives and optional modules used by Bitcoin software. It is intentionally narrow infrastructure rather than a wallet or node. The library is maintained in the Bitcoin Core GitHub organization, publishes signed releases, and is reused widely across the Bitcoin ecosystem. Version 0.7.1 was released January 26, 2026.
records.Launch / history: The library grew out of Bitcoin Core cryptographic engineering and became a reusable standalone project. Version 0.7.1 was current in January 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a foundational cryptographic dependency whose correctness and performance affect a large share of Bitcoin implementations without itself defining network policy or application behavior.
records.Verification basis: Official Bitcoin Core repository and 0.7.1 release history establish active maintenance and cryptographic-library scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply this library alone defines Bitcoin consensus; consensus validation is broader than cryptographic signature primitives.
Downstream projects may pin different versions or bindings.

records.Concise description: A long-running cross-platform C++ toolkit for building Bitcoin applications and protocol software.
records.Deeper researched summary: Libbitcoin is a family of C++ libraries centered on libbitcoin-system, providing Bitcoin data structures, serialization, cryptographic integration, and higher-level development components. The canonical repository is actively maintained in 2026. MSC consolidates the toolkit and its server/client lineage into one profile rather than splitting every Libbitcoin component, while recognizing its historical importance as an alternative Bitcoin development stack.
records.Launch / history: Libbitcoin dates to the early 2010s and evolved into a multi-library C++ toolkit. The canonical libbitcoin-system repository showed active pushes on August 15, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of Bitcoin's longest-lived non-Core developer library ecosystems and provides meaningful implementation diversity for protocol/application development.
records.Verification basis: Current project-controlled repository activity on 2026-08-15 and official toolkit documentation establish an active library ecosystem.
Research notes / uncertainties: MSC consolidates Libbitcoin components into one profile to avoid dependency-directory padding.
Do not present old libbitcoin-server deployment assumptions as current unless separately reverified.

records.Concise description: A mature Java/JVM library for Bitcoin protocol networking, lightweight/SPV operation, wallet construction, transaction handling, and application integration.
records.Deeper researched summary: bitcoinj provides Bitcoin protocol types, networking, wallet APIs, and lightweight synchronization for JVM applications. Its documentation emphasizes SPV-style lightweight operation while also documenting experimental full-verification capabilities. The current website documents API version 0.17.1, and the GitHub organization shows active 2026 maintenance. Because its canonical role is reusable Bitcoin infrastructure rather than a specific end-user wallet, NETWORK is the appropriate home.
records.Launch / history: bitcoinj was created in 2011 and became foundational to multiple early Bitcoin applications. It remains maintained, with 0.17.1 current documentation and active 2026 repository work.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the oldest durable non-Core Bitcoin libraries and brought Bitcoin networking and wallet primitives to the Java/JVM ecosystem.
records.Verification basis: Current official site documents 0.17.1 APIs and project scope; 2026 GitHub organization activity supports ACTIVE classification.
Research notes / uncertainties: SPV/lightweight security assumptions differ from full-node validation; do not describe lightweight mode as equivalent to a fully validating node.
Wallet APIs are library functionality, not a separate canonical end-user wallet profile.
